headline: Peruvian sol weakens to S/3.458 per dollar amid lower copper prices
summary: The US dollar advanced 0.23% against the Peruvian sol to close at S/3.458 in Lima, pressured by falling copper prices and heightened international risk aversion.
why: Peru is the world's third-largest copper producer, making the sol particularly responsive to global commodity pricing and broader emerging-market sentiment.

impacts.name: Peruvian Sol
impacts.why: The sol depreciated to S/3.458 as copper prices declined and international investors shed risk.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A drop in global copper quotations coupled with international risk aversion weighed on the Peruvian currency during Friday's trading session.
